topic: Assessing whether an idea is novel and non-obvious before expanding it (Graham v. John Deere / MPEP 2141 adapted for engineering judgment, NOVEL/BORDERLINE/NOT-NOVEL verdicts)

subtopics.scope: The Graham v. John Deere obviousness framework: 35 U.S.C. 103, the four inquiries codified in MPEP 2141, and how they map onto engineering judgment.
seed_queries: Graham v. John Deere obviousness framework four inquiries

subtopics.scope: The KSR v. Teleflex rationale catalog (MPEP 2141 III): the six rejection rationales A through F, which are strongest, and how to anticipate a 103 rejection of an engineering idea.
seed_queries: KSR v. Teleflex obviousness rationale combining prior art elements
MPEP 2141 III KSR rationale obvious to try rejection

subtopics.scope: Splitting an idea into mechanism / trigger / policy layers: why the combination is what patent law treats as the invention, and how engineering novelty often lives in one layer only.
seed_queries: mechanism trigger policy layer decomposition of a system idea
separating mechanism from application novelty engineering

subtopics.scope: Checking the project's own ADRs, PRs, Linear issues, and refs/ docs as the first and highest-signal prior-art source before any external scan.
seed_queries: architecture decision records as internal prior art before building
checking existing pull requests and issues for duplicate feature work

subtopics.scope: External prior-art scanning for engineering judgment: direct equivalents, failed and abandoned attempts, academic and formal work, adjacent or historical efforts.
seed_queries: prior art search methodology direct equivalents failed attempts
how to survey existing solutions before building new feature academic and industry

subtopics.scope: Level of ordinary skill in the pertinent art (PHOSITA): could a skilled practitioner combine the known elements; the obvious-to-try standard.
seed_queries: person having ordinary skill in the art PHOSITA definition level of skill
obvious to try standard patent law finite number of predictable solutions

subtopics.scope: Secondary considerations (objective indicia): long-felt need, failure of others, unexpected results, and why they only count with evidence.
seed_queries: secondary considerations nonobviousness long felt need failure of others
objective indicia of nonobviousness unexpected results evidence

subtopics.scope: The verdict taxonomy (NOVEL / BORDERLINE / NOT-NOVEL), the output document template, anti-patterns, red flags, and the verification checklist. Source-doc-grounded; internal-record subtopic, no dig.
